tasks.title: The History of Photography
paras: The history of photography is marked by significant technological progress and artistic innovation. It began in the early nineteenth century with the invention of the camera obscura, a device that projected images onto a surface. The first permanent photograph was created by Joseph-Nicéphore Niépce in 1826 using a process called heliography, which required several hours of exposure to light. Photography quickly evolved with the development of daguerreotypes, introduced by Louis Daguerre in 1839. This method produced detailed images on silver-plated copper, but daguerreotypes needed delicate handling, and the exposure times required, although much shorter, still remained impractical for recording images of moving objects. The invention of the calotype by William Henry Fox Talbot in the 1840s allowed for multiple copies of an image to be made from a single negative, revolutionizing the field. (A)In the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, the introduction of film and roll cameras made photography more accessible to the public. (B)George Eastman’s establishment of the Kodak company in 1888 played a crucial role in this democratization, as his cameras were simple to use and affordable. (C)Today, digital photography has further transformed the medium, allowing instant image capture and sharing.(D)

questions.stem: The word “innovation” in the passage is closest in meaning to
questions.analysis: 正确答案：B 题型： 词汇题 原文定位： “The history of photography is marked by significant technological progress and artistic innovation.” 正确答案分析： “innovation” 意为“创新、革新”，在上下文中与 “progress”（进步）并列，都表示积极的发展。因此 “advancement”（进步、发展）是最接近的含义。 选项分析： (A) success 成功 —— 语义过宽，不完全等同。 (B) advancement 进步 —— 正确。 (C) activity 活动 —— 无关。 (D) expression 表达 —— 无关。

options.A: They were introduced by Joseph-Nicéphore Niépce.
options.B: They allowed for multiple copies of an image.
options.C: They required shorter exposure times than heliographs did.
options.D: They made it unnecessary to use silver-plated copper.

questions.analysis: 正确答案：C 题型： 细节题 原文定位： “This method produced detailed images on silver-plated copper, but daguerreotypes needed delicate handling, and the exposure times required, although much shorter, still remained impractical for recording images of moving objects.” 正确答案分析： 文中明确提到 daguerreotypes 的曝光时间 “although much shorter” 比之前的 heliography（需数小时）短得多，因此选项 C 正确。 选项分析： (A) They were introduced by Joseph-Nicéphore Niépce. —— 错误，daguerreotypes 由 Louis Daguerre 引入。 (B) They allowed for multiple copies of an image. —— 错误，这是 calotype 的特点。 (C) They required shorter exposure times than heliographs did. —— 正确。 (D) They made it unnecessary to use silver-plated copper. —— 错误，daguerreotypes 正是在银镀铜上制作的。

questions.stem: How did the calotype revolutionize photography?

options.B: By reducing the need for delicate handling
options.C: By providing detailed images on silver-plated copper
options.D: By allowing multiple copies from a single negative

questions.analysis: 正确答案：D 题型： 细节题 原文定位： “The invention of the calotype by William Henry Fox Talbot in the 1840s allowed for multiple copies of an image to be made from a single negative, revolutionizing the field.” 正确答案分析： 文中明确指出 calotype 的革命性在于允许从一张底片制作多张拷贝，这正是选项 D 的内容。 选项分析： (A) By enabling instant image capture —— 错误，这是数字摄影的特点。 (B) By reducing the need for delicate handling —— 错误，文中未提及 calotype 有此特点。 (C) By providing detailed images on silver-plated copper —— 错误，这是 daguerreotypes 的特点。 (D) By allowing multiple copies from a single negative —— 正确。

questions.stem: Why does the author mention George Eastman’s establishment of the Kodak company?

options.A: To highlight the role of Kodak in making photography accessible to the public
options.B: To criticize the challenges of early photographic methods
options.C: To explain how ﬁlm was invented
options.D: To suggest that Kodak introduced digital photography

questions.analysis: 正确答案：A 题型： 修辞目的题 原文定位： “George Eastman’s establishment of the Kodak company in 1888 played a crucial role in this democratization, as his cameras were simple to use and affordable.” 正确答案分析： 作者提到柯达公司是为了说明它如何推动摄影的 “democratization”（大众化），即让公众更容易接触摄影。选项 A 准确表达了这一目的。 选项分析： (A) To highlight the role of Kodak in making photography accessible to the public —— 正确。 (B) To criticize the challenges of early photographic methods —— 错误，无批评之意。 (C) To explain how film was invented —— 错误，未解释胶片发明过程。 (D) To suggest that Kodak introduced digital photography —— 错误，柯达引入的是胶片相机，非数字摄影。

questions.stem: There are four locations (A, B, C, and D) in the passage that indicate where the following sentence could be added. These developments have rendered the use of film and many types of cameras obsolete. Where would the sentence best fit? Select a location where the sentence could be added to the passage.
questions.analysis: 正确答案：D 题型： 句子插入题 原文定位（各选项所在句子）： (A) 位于：“The invention of the calotype... revolutionizing the field. (A) In the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, the introduction of film and roll cameras made photography more accessible to the public.” (B) 位于：“...made photography more accessible to the public. (B) George Eastman’s establishment of the Kodak company in 1888 played a crucial role in this democratization, as his cameras were simple to use and affordable.” (C) 位于：“...simple to use and affordable. (C) Today, digital photography has further transformed the medium, allowing instant image capture and sharing.” (D) 位于：“...allowing instant image capture and sharing. (D) [段落结束]” 正确答案分析： 待插入句子 “These developments have rendered the use of film and many types of cameras obsolete.” 意为“这些发展使胶片和许多类型的相机过时”。其中的 “these developments” 应指代前文提到的数字摄影等新技术。数字摄影的出现使胶片和许多相机过时，因此应放在介绍数字摄影的句子之后，即 (D) 位置，作为段落的总结句。 选项分析： (A) 错误 —— 前文是 calotype，胶片尚未普及，说过时为时过早。 (B) 错误 —— 前文是胶片相机的普及，此时数字摄影尚未出现。 (C) 错误 —— 若插入在此，后文才讲数字摄影，逻辑顺序混乱。 (D) 正确 —— 位于数字摄影介绍之后，指代清晰，逻辑连贯。
